correctness.rationale: The nested-fan and search-tree correspondence translates all Gaussian directions into n! equiprobable strict coordinate orders. Each labeled biclique broom has precisely r! permutations, and the two exhaustion-color cases count all brooms without overlap. All finite formulas and normalization follow. In balanced dimensions, dominated convergence establishes vertex-count/typical sampling limits. The exact collision summands a_m(k) have fixed-k limit 1/k! and ratio (m+k)/((m-k)(k+1)); an explicit factorial majorant plus a monotone tail shows their sum converges to e, proving the collision probability and conditional Poisson law. The standalone exhaustive checker passed eight parameter pairs and exact collision identities. No finite check is substituted for proof of limits.

value.rationale: A Gaussian exposing direction is a canonical intrinsic geometric sampling procedure for polytopes. The exact angular census distinguishes this geometry from uniform vertex counting. The rare-event asymptotic shows a striking separation: normal Gaussian selection has O(1) leaves, uniform vertices have a positive conditioned Poisson(1/2) leaf count, while collisions overwhelmingly require r=m-O(1) and a Poisson(1) deficit. This quantifies a previously unaccounted geometric selection bias and a naturally motivated collision invariant for an infinite well-studied family; it is not an arbitrary fixed parameter slice or a recoding of a known finite table.
